input: Set up a direct debit for the council tax bill

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The process for setting up a direct debit varies by local council — online portals, phone lines, and paper forms differ between authorities, so knowing which council is involved determines the exact steps.
Council tax direct debits can cover a full year or be split across 10 or 12 monthly instalments, and the payment date options vary — this changes what the user needs to select during setup.
The user may want to set this up online, by phone, or by post — their preferred channel determines which instructions to follow and what materials to prepare.
If the bill is in joint names or a partner/housemate is also responsible, the account holder details and bank account used may need to match or involve another person.
If a payment is already overdue or a deadline is approaching, the urgency changes the plan — the user may need to make a one-off payment first before the direct debit kicks in.
Some users just need the direct debit confirmed and active; others also want to verify the amount, check the first payment date, or receive written confirmation — this shapes what 'done' looks like.
The user may already have an online council account set up, or may never have registered — this affects whether account creation is a prerequisite step in the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Set up council tax direct debit payment
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to arrange an automatic direct debit to pay their council tax bill to their local council.

questions.title: Which local council is your bill with?
questions.description: Identify the specific local authority issuing the council tax bill, as each council has its own process and portal for setting up direct debits.

questions.title: How many monthly instalments do you want to pay over?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants to spread payments over 10 or 12 months, or pay in full — this affects what options to select during setup.

questions.title: Do you want to set this up online, by phone, or by post?
questions.description: Establish the user's preferred channel for setting up the direct debit, as the steps differ significantly between methods.

questions.title: Is the council tax bill solely in your name?
questions.description: Clarify whether the account is in one name or shared, as joint liability may require both parties' details or a jointly held bank account.

questions.title: Is any payment currently overdue or due very soon?
questions.description: Check whether there is an urgent or missed payment, which may require a one-off payment before the direct debit is active.

questions.title: Do you already have an online account with your council?
questions.description: Determine whether account registration is a prerequisite step, or if the user can proceed directly to the direct debit setup.

questions.title: What does success look like — confirmation email, first payment taken, or something else?
questions.description: Understand what the user considers the task complete, such as receiving written confirmation, seeing the direct debit on their bank account, or something more specific.
